catalog_quote: The phonological word (PW) in Ketengban is the domain of one stress. The stressed syllable is frequently, but not always, accompanied by higher pitch than the non-stressed syllables. The majority of PWs consist of one to three syllables although words of up to five syllables are known to occur. 1.1 Stress. Stress is phonemic, as evidenced by the following contrasts: Between nouns: /'bume/ ['bumɛ] 'horsefly' /bu'me/ [bu'mɛ] 'short' /'kalum/ ['kalum] 'charcoal' /ka'lum/ [ka'lum] 'tapioca type' Between noun and verb: /'bana/ ['bana] 'to walk' /ba'na/ [ba'na] 'jaw' /'galuna/ ['galuna] 'vegetable type' /ga'luna/ [ga'luna] 'to wear net bag with base on head' ... Between verbs: /'kouna/ ... 'to bundle up' /kou'na/ ... 'to plant' ... 1.2 Shape of the Phonological Word. PWs exhibit the following syllable and stress patterns: One-syllable words: 'S ... (2) Deciding source: a 1982 SIL working-paper phonology (25 pp.) with an explicit, example-rich stress section — minimal pairs across nouns and verbs and a stress-position inventory for 1-5 syllable words showing stress on any syllable — which is exactly the evidence type a lexical coding needs. Glottolog's complete 26-item bibliography (downloaded now) lists no grammar, no sketch, and no other phonology; MPI-EVA/Crossref show no later phonological or instrumental study. tone.quote: Stress seems to be partially phonemic in the east, e.g. Ok Bab ‘uku 'fire' and uku young plant of sweet potatoes', while tones are said to be phonemic in Nalca and Kosarek (Bromley 1973:15 and Rule and Cutting). ... In all the examples I have collected syllable contraction is involved in the development of tonal features and this contraction in the west presupposes stress to the east ... Thus tonal features develop only in certain restricted environments, and the tonal analysis of Nalca and Kosarek may be partly right, though, due to the restrictions, tones have to be marked only on a very limited set of the vocabulary.
tone.locator: pp. 12-13, section 1.2 'Diversity of the Mek languages'
tone.summary: No tone posited for Ketengban (eastern Mek): word stress is (partially) phonemic there; phonemic tone is attributed only to western Mek (Nalca, Kosarek) and explained as a secondary development from syllable contraction and final glottal loss, with eastern stress as the older state.
